data.title: Catena Media announces preliminary Q3 results and financial target update
data.description:
Catena Media plc today publishes preliminary, unaudited results for the third quarter of 2026, together with a non-cash impairment charge and an update to the group’s 2026 financial targets.

Preliminary Q3 revenue was EUR 8.3m, down 29 percent from the same period last year (11.6m). Revenue for the first nine months was EUR 30.1m (31.0m). Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was EUR 0.7m (2.9m), including a reversal of EUR 0.7m of accruals made earlier in the year for the 2026 employee bonus programme. Adjusted EBITDA for the first nine months was EUR 4.6m (5.2m).

Given the above, the group no longer expects to reach its target of double-digit organic growth in group revenue and adjusted EBITDA in 2026.

Catena Media expects to recognise a non-cash impairment charge on intangible assets of EUR 30-35m in Q3, in accordance with IAS 36.

Several factors adversely affected operating performance in Q3. Generative search continued to transform how users discover brands online, reducing new traffic across the affiliate industry. Catena Media's traditional search rankings declined, due both to AI-assisted personalised search patterns and also to search engines continuing to elevate lower-relevancy content in search results. Certain operators also reduced their marketing budgets during the usual seasonal summer slowdown.

Since Catena Media acquires more than 90 percent of new customers under cost-per-acquisition (CPA) deals, the group has limited recurring revenue to buffer against such a combination of market pressures.

Manuel Stan, Catena Media CEO, commented: “This was a weak quarter and our results reflect that. The search landscape is undergoing a rapid and fundamental shift, and as a predominantly CPA-based business our results reflect the effects of these changes immediately and in full.

“The results reinforce the strategic direction we set out in the second quarter. We are reducing our dependence on search by diversifying our revenue streams, including through our newly announced TraffiqX project and new verticals like prediction markets, and by continuing to build the strength of our brands through investing in customer loyalty programmes. These efforts will be further supported by TraffiqX, the new platform we plan to launch in the first quarter of 2027.”

All figures in this release are preliminary and unaudited. Catena Media will publish its interim report for Q3 2026 on 10 November at 17:35 CET, followed by a webcast at 18:00 CET: https://events.inderes.com/catena-media/q3-report-2026

data.title: Nasdaq Pulls Back Sharply But Dow Seeing Further Upside
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Extending recent volatility on Wall Street, the major U.S. stock indexes have moved in notably opposite directions during trading on Friday.

While the tech-heavy Nasdaq has moved sharply lower, the Dow is adding to yesterday's strong gain, reaching its best intraday level in almost a month.

Currently, the Nasdaq is just off its low of the session, down 279.18 points or 1.1 percent at 26,433.85. The S&P 500 is also down 23.25 points or 0.3 percent at 7,720.81, but the Dow is up 188.62 points or 0.4 percent at 52,366.31.

Financial giant JPMorgan Chase (JPM) has helped lead the Dow higher, jumping by 2.5 percent. Home Depot (HD), American Express (AXP) and Disney (DIS) are also posting strong gains.

Meanwhile, renewed weakness among technology stocks is weighing on the Nasdaq amid concerns about debt-fueled AI infrastructure spending.

Computer hardware stocks are turning in some of the tech sector's worst performances, extending the nosedive seen over the past couple weeks, with the NYSE Arca Computer Hardware Index plunging by 3.2 percent.

Software, networking and semiconductor stocks are also seeing significant weakness, contributing to the slump by the Nasdaq.

Outside of the tech sector, gold stocks are seeing further upside along with the price of the precious metal, driving the NYSE Arca Gold Bugs Index up by 1.7 percent.

Banking, housing and utilities stocks are also seeing notable strength, possibly benefiting from a rotation out of tech stocks.

On the U.S. economic front, a report released by the Federal Reserve showed industrial production in the U.S. increased by more than expected in the month of September.

The Fed said industrial production climbed by 0.7 percent in September following a revised 0.1 percent uptick in August.

Economists had expected industrial production to rise by 0.4 percent compared to the unchanged reading originally reported for the previous month.

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved mostly higher during trading on Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index jumped by 1.4 percent, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index climbed by 0.5 percent.

The major European markets have also moved to the upside on the day. The German DAX Index is up by 1.1 percent, the French CAC 40 Index is up by 0.4 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index is up by 0.3 percent.

In the bond market, treasuries are seeing modest strength following yesterday's rally. As a result, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its, is down by 1.2 basis points at 5.075 percent.

data.title: Lilly’s Foundayo Pill Gets European Regulatory Backing – LLY Stock Heads For Best Week In Nearly Four Months
data.description:
Key points:
  • The EMA’s advisory committee recommended approving Foundayo for adults with obesity or those who are overweight and have related health conditions.
  • The committee also backed its use in adults with type 2 diabetes.
  • Foundayo generated $98 million in Q2 revenue.

Eli Lilly (LLY) received a boost to its European business after the European Medicines Agency’s (EMA) advisory committee recommended approval of its once-daily weight-loss pill, Foundayo, on Friday.

The recommendation comes as Lilly looks to build on the success of its blockbuster weight-loss treatments, Mounjaro and Zepbound.

LLY shares were up 1.8% at the time of writing. The stock has gained about 7.8% so far this week, heading for its best weekly gain in nearly four months.

Foundayo Moves Closer To European Launch

The EMA’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended approving Foundayo for adults with obesity or those who are overweight and have related health conditions. The committee also backed its use in adults with type 2 diabetes.

Foundayo contains Orforglipron, which helps control blood sugar and reduce appetite. Unlike some oral GLP-1 treatments, it can be taken without food or water restrictions.

The pill is already available in the U.S., the U.K. and the United Arab Emirates. In the U.S., it received FDA approval in April for weight management, while in the U.K., it received approval in August for both weight management and type 2 diabetes.

What Happens Next?

Foundayo still requires final authorization from the European Commission, which generally issues a decision within 67 days of EMA’s recommendation. While the timeline puts a potential decision around late December, Lilly has not confirmed when commercial sales would begin.

Foundayo generated $98 million in second-quarter (Q2) revenue. However, Lilly's two blockbuster drugs generated far more. In Q2, Mounjaro generated $9.94 billion in sales, up 91% year over year, while Zepbound brought in $4.93 billion, up 46%.

Retail Says LLY Is Breaking Out

Retail sentiment surrounding LLY on Stocktwits turned ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish’ over the past 24 hours, though message volumes remained ‘normal.’

One user noted that LLY stock is breaking out.

View this Stocktwits post

LLY shares have gained more than 18% so far this year, significantly outperforming rival Novo Nordisk (NVO), whose shares have slumped more than 25% over the same period.

data.title: SpaceX's spectrum deal still leaves it far from rivaling telecom giants
data.description:
Key points:
  • SpaceX agrees to buy Grain's nationwide 800 MHz portfolio for about $8 billion, a source says
  • Portfolio includes up to 14 MHz of paired spectrum and needs FCC approval
  • TD Cowen estimates nationwide terrestrial network would cost more than $80 billion

By Harshita Mary Varghese

SpaceX called its recent multibillion-dollar purchase of US airwaves a critical step towards building a mobile network, but constructing a true rival to major American carriers will require a terrestrial network and likely years of work and billions more.

Starlink became a money maker by offering internet service in rural and sparsely populated areas, where it faced little competition, as well as changing to easy-to-set-up home packages at a competitive price. Mobile will be harder.

Cities are particularly tough places for mobile telephony and are technologically challenging for mobile-to-satellite connections.

The rocket and satellite company will likely need to invest heavily in ground infrastructure, customer service, handset subsidies and promotions — costly parts of the wireless business in which AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile already have extensive operations.

Building a network would cost more than $80 billion, according to TD Cowen, and add to SpaceX's capital demands as it pours money into its Starship rocket program, AI infrastructure, and Terafab chip factory.

"It's just hard to imagine that this is all going to get done within a decade," said Julie Zhu, a research analyst at MoffettNathanson. "In the decade or so leading up to 2023, the big three spent about $650 billion in capex to build in networks that ostensibly were already finished."

Most phones have small antennas and limited transmitting power that make reliable satellite connections more challenging because satellites orbit hundreds of kilometers above Earth, much farther away than cell towers.

"There are too many pitfalls for satellite to be the only source of data," said Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy.

SPACEX PUBLISHES HYBRID SPACE-TERRESTRIAL PLAN

SpaceX has called the latest deal, in which it acquired 800 MHz spectrum licenses from Grain at a price a source pegged at nearly $8 billion, a "critical next step" for the nascent Starlink Mobile to provide high-speed mobile service.

"Starlink Mobile will deploy a flexible architecture combining our satellite-to-mobile constellation in space with an advanced terrestrial deployment that can seamlessly connect devices everywhere," including "indoors, outdoors, in cellular dead zones, and everywhere in between", SpaceX said, announcing the purchase.

SpaceX has received regulatory authorization for up to 15,000 Starlink Mobile satellites and plans to deploy traditional terrestrial infrastructure such as antennas on towers and rooftops — a hybrid approach rather than pure satellite-to-phone — it laid out in a regulatory filing made public last week.

In a Starlink Mobile system, satellites could connect directly to mobile phones and indirectly by relaying signals through ground infrastructure. This is similar to the technology of a partnership between Starlink and T-Mobile, which provides the terrestrial network while Starlink supplies the satellite connectivity that fills in where there are no towers. That is a T-Mobile-branded service.

SpaceX in theory could strike a deal with one of the big three companies to use its ground infrastructure, what is known as a mobile virtual network operator, or MVNO, arrangement. However, SpaceX "appear to be going after a more build-your-own approach to a terrestrial network since nobody will offer them wholesale MVNO," Sag said.

SpaceX would need several times more spectrum to match the holdings of the three big mobile companies, although current spectrum might be enough to start. "It is for a company with zero mobile subscribers, plenty of runway, and a robust device/equipment ecosystem," TD Cowen said.

Would-be rivals dismissed the idea that the effort was an imminent threat.

T-Mobile Chief Technology Officer John Saw said SpaceX's spectrum would not be enough to match the capacity and performance of established mobile networks, while Katie Magnotta, Verizon's associate vice president of corporate communications, said, "A company can have billions of dollars of spectrum, but if they do not have the network to use it, it's just empty airwaves."

data.title: IMF Chief Says AI Is Strengthening Global Economy — But Warns Delayed Productivity Gains Could Trigger Shocks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Hyperscalers’ share of investment-grade bond issuance has risen more than tenfold over the past two years, according to the IMF.
  • A major cyberattack on payment and trading systems, or on access to deposits, could cause immediate losses and undermine confidence, according to Georgieva.
  • U.S. Treasury Undersecretary Erin Browne argued the IMF should give greater weight to AI’s potential for positive economic shocks, Reuters reported.

International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned Friday that artificial intelligence (AI) could trigger negative economic shocks if anticipated productivity gains take longer than expected, even as the technology strengthens global growth.

Speaking at an IMF-World Bank panel in Bangkok alongside Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark, Georgieva said, "If there are no safeguards, then the risks may exceed the opportunities.”

“Above all, we do need an ethical foundation, ​and I'm not sure we are there as a society," the IMF chief added.

Georgieva Calls For AI Safeguards

Georgieva advocated a combination of industry self-regulation and government involvement, including from the U.S., China and India. She highlighted access to electricity and digital infrastructure as essential to ensuring AI's benefits are widely shared.

Harvard economist Dani Rodrik also reiterated Georgieva's warning that disappointing productivity gains could result in a costly financial correction following substantial data-center investments.

IMF Flags Growing Hyperscaler Debt, Circular Financing Risks

In an IMF blog titled "The World Can't Afford to Get AI Wrong," Georgieva highlighted growing financial risks stemming from hyperscalers' increasing reliance on debt to fund AI infrastructure.

Their share of investment-grade bond issuance has increased more than tenfold in two years, rising from less than 1% to 10% and growing, according to the blog.

Georgieva also warned about circular financing arrangements in which hyperscalers invest in AI developers that subsequently purchase computing capacity from those same companies.

The IMF's October report examined 14 such transactions since 2023, identifying approximately $300 billion in equity investments and $650 billion in debt tied to $1.4 trillion in future revenue commitments.

Earnings Disappointments, Cyberattacks Could Pressure Valuations

Georgieva's blog warned that significant revenue or earnings disappointments by AI developers could undermine profitability expectations and pressure equity valuations.

A severe correction could spread through the leveraged, interconnected AI ecosystem, with losses potentially reaching global investors, the blog warned.

She also noted that AI-powered cyberattacks targeting payments, trading systems or access to bank deposits could cause immediate losses and undermine financial confidence.

However, the IMF estimated that AI could boost annual global economic growth by roughly half a percentage point over the next decade if productivity improvements materialize.

Meanwhile, Reuters reported that U.S. Treasury Undersecretary Erin Browne pushed back against the IMF's emphasis on downside risks, arguing that the fund should give greater weight to AI's potential to deliver positive economic shocks.

data.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case, a close relative of other two cases
data.description:
Kenya has confirmed a third Ebola case in a close relative of the first and second cases, the health ministry said on Friday.

The ministry said in a statement that the third case was a 65-year-old woman who had been in quarantine since October 6.

"Once she developed fever, sore throat and malaise, she was isolated and specimen collected for testing. She tested positive for Ebola," the statement said, adding: "She was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care improving her chances of recovery."

Kenya's cases are linked to the Ebola epidemic in Congo, which is the second-largest on record globally with more than 9,000 cases and over 4,000 deaths.

Kenya's first case emerged last week after a Kenyan man, who had been ill in Congo about a month before travelling by road to Uganda, flew to Nairobi on October 3, where a relative drove him to the hospital. He died on October 5.

data.title: World's rarest porpoise battles extinction as Mexico shrinks protected area
data.description:
Key points:
  • New agreement cuts vaquita's protected area by 86%
  • Gov't says smaller area will help fishermen
  • Only 7 to 10 vaquitas left in Gulf of California
  • Scientists hope for better enforcement to prevent extinction

By Ana Isabel Martinez and Sarah Morland

Mexico's president said on Thursday a drastic reduction in the protected area for the near-extinct vaquita marina, the world's smallest porpoise, will help fishing communities.

Critics say this week's reduction in the area where fishermen cannot use gillnets, long walls of nylon mesh, by 86% to 1,562 square kilometers (603 square miles), about the size of Greater London, threatens the survival of the species.

The prior agreement had protected an area similar to the size of the US state of Connecticut.

President Claudia Sheinbaum said the new scope aimed to protect biodiversity in the Gulf of California while also allowing fishermen to make a better living.

Authorities said the measure took into account proposals by the International Committee for the Recovery of the Vaquita, a government advisory body.

Lorenzo Rojas-Bracho, a Mexican marine biologist and leading vaquita expert who took part in the committee, said he hoped a smaller area could concentrate efforts to save the mammal.

"It is difficult to enforce a ban over a very large area, which includes vast areas with no recent records of vaquitas," Rojas-Bracho told Reuters. "If you lose a ring you don't search your entire house, you focus on where you lost it."

Scientists estimated last year there were just 7 to 10 vaquitas left, including at least one calf. The population has collapsed from around 600 in 1997, largely due to illegal fishing targeting totoaba, whose swim bladders are highly prized in Chinese medicine and can fetch up to $10,000 in Asia.

Rojas-Bracho said that if no more vaquitas are killed, the remaining handful of porpoises would have a good chance of repopulating the species.

However, he said the area needs more effective tracking of fishing boats, better monitoring and that fishermen should use alternative methods that do not put the vaquita at risk.

Gerardo Ceballos, a biologist at the National Autonomous University of Mexico, said allowing the vaquita to become extinct would amount to a moral failure.

"What's happening to the vaquita is a death foretold," he said. "We've reduced the vaquita's protected area without actually having the technical or logistical capacity to enforce regulations there; we're giving in to pressure from interested groups so a larger area can be exploited."

Ceballos said a very minimal government investment would ensure the vaquita's protection. As things currently stood, however, he believed the porpoise was on the path to extinction.

"If the vaquita goes extinct it won't solve insecurity or poverty or any of the local problems. And Mexico would lose an icon," he said. "If actions are taken, there is a possibility, a hope. And we must keep working with hope."

data.title: Technical Execution, Timing Seen Key for Quantum Computing Race — Market Talk
data.description: It's an open question as to which quantum computing company is positioned to lead a market expected to reach $10 billion in 2030, Morgan Stanley analysts write in a note. If fault-tolerant quantum computers become widely commercially adopted, that market could grow to $100 billion by 2040, they project. Still, everything hinges on technical execution and timing: each quantum company in Morgan Stanley's coverage has a milestone set for 2027, with fault-tolerant systems expected in 2029 or 2030 per company roadmaps. "Today's revenue is too small to show which businesses will succeed," the analysts write. "The investment question is which companies are most likely to reach fault tolerance first." (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

data.title: Polymarket Bitcoin and Rate Hike Odds Shift as CME Says No Change
data.description:
Polymarket put the odds of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in October at 23%, with $43 million traded, while CME FedWatch pricing ranged from roughly 37% to 44%, and the gap formed as Bitcoin fell below $82,000 following hotter-than-expected inflation data, though it is recovering. Polymarket vs.

The September consumer price index rose 3.7% year over year, above the 3.6% consensus and August’s 3.4%, according to the October 15 market report. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, also came in above expectations: it increased 0.3% month over month against a 0.2% forecast, and 2.6% annually against 2.5% expected. Gasoline prices rose 9.1% on the month.

The report pushed FedWatch’s October hike probability from about 22% before the release to approximately 37%-44% during Wednesday. Polymarket’s price moved more modestly, from 20% late Tuesday to 24% in the report’s snapshot. Bitcoin (BTC)24h7d30d1yAll time

The macro repricing had a direct risk-asset channel: expectations of higher interest rates can lift financing costs and weigh on liquidity, reducing the appeal of assets that do not yield cash flows. Bitcoin fell below $82,000, while Ether dropped about 3% to near $2,430.

The Federal Reserve had raised its target range to 3.75%-4% in September, its first increase since 2023. Its next meeting is scheduled for October 27-28, leaving traders to assess whether the latest data warrants another immediate move or gives policymakers reason to wait.The Federal Reserve building in Washington, DC. – Photo: bettrichard873Earn $50 and Enter $300K Prize Draw on EdgeXOctober or December is The Bigger Test for Bitcoin?

Polymarket’s contract asks whether the Fed will raise rates by 25 basis points after the October meeting. FedWatch reflects expectations derived from fed funds futures. Both offer a market-based reading of the same decision.

MeasureReported probabilityTiming
Polymarket: October hike24%Oct. 15 report snapshot
CME FedWatch: October hike37%-44%Wednesday, Oct. 14
Polymarket: October hike13.5%Oct. 16
Polymarket: December hike79%Oct. 15

The calendar complicates the October call. The meeting falls six days before the November 3 midterm elections; UBS described a move so close to the vote as politically untenable, Reuters reported the Fed might wait until December, and Capital Economics considered an October hike possible.

The October report’s own analysis put a fair probability for a hike closer to 35%, above Polymarket’s 24% but below the upper end of the FedWatch range. More important for the broader policy path, Polymarket priced a December hike at 79%: an October hold could therefore mean delay rather than a change in the market’s expectation of further tightening.

That distinction matters to Bitcoin. If the Fed holds in October while December expectations remain elevated, the immediate risk of another hike recedes, but the prospect of tighter policy later may still constrain liquidity and limit any relief in risk assets.

The relationship between policy expectations and Treasury real rates is one relevant macro channel, though these probabilities do not establish how Bitcoin will respond.

Got a Gut Feeling? It Could Pay Out 3.7X on PolymarketBitcoin Turns Defensive on Polymarket Rate Hike Odds

Polymarket’s Bitcoin contracts reflected a sharp shift in sentiment across the 24 hours to late Wednesday. The probability of Bitcoin reaching $85,000 in October fell from 83% to 63%, while the chance of reaching $87,500 dropped from 56% to 39%. In the opposite direction, the probability of a dip to $77,500 rose from 30% to 37%.What price will Bitcoin hit in October? Polymarket

Those prices describe what participants were willing to pay for specific outcomes at that time. A Bitcoin recovery case remains conditional on both price action and the next changes in rate expectations.

The next formal decision point is the October 27-28 meeting; until then, the sharp change in Polymarket pricing from 24% on Thursday to 13.5% on Friday shows why traders need to keep the timestamp attached to every probability.

data.description:
West African crude differentials were steady on Friday against a broader backdrop of trending lower, as traders digested tender results.

  • India's IOC bought cargoes of Nemba, Sangos and Djeno in a recent tender, one trader said.

  • West African crudes have faced pressure this week as record-high freight rates have hampered demand for grades that usually travel long-haul to their main demand outlets.

  • That has affected Angolan grades more than Nigerian crudes so far, a trader said.

  • A drop in values in the Mediterranean and North Sea markets could further weigh on West African grades as the overall oil complex weakens, another trader added.

  • Many cargoes remain unsold in the current cycle, ahead of the release of December programmes, the trader said.

  • Market participants were awaiting Angola's December loading schedule on Friday.

data.title: NEC exhibits at the 32nd ITS World Congress, a conference and exhibition focused on mobility
data.description:
TOKYO, Oct 16, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - NEC Corporation (NEC; TSE: 6701) has announced its participation in the upcoming 32nd ITS World Congress as an exhibitor at the ITS Japan Pavilion, which will showcase public- and private-sector exhibitors affiliated with ITS Japan. Additionally, NEC will present a technical paper during a session at the event. This five-day conference and exhibition, which brings together experts from industry, government, and academia, focuses on intelligent transport systems (ITS) and will be held in Gangneung, Korea, from October 19 (Monday) to October 23 (Friday), 2026 (ITS Japan Pavilion; Booth number: S25).

The ITS World Congress, which aims to solve road traffic problems through the widespread adoption of ITS and to create business opportunities, is the only world congress co-organized annually by three key ITS organizations from around the globe (Europe: ERTICO; the Americas: ITS America; the Asia-Pacific region: ITS Asia-Pacific). This event features a vast variety of technical sessions, exhibits, panel discussions and more, serving as a forum for participants to exchange information from diverse perspectives on a wide range of topics, including technological development and market trends.

Exhibit Overview

Based on the concept of "Shaping the Mobility of Tomorrow," NEC aims to harness ICT and utilize road infrastructure and related data to create new environmentally friendly mobility services that ensure safety, security, and convenience. Moreover, the data collected through these services will be integrated and used to facilitate smarter, more sustainable and efficient transportation.

At this year's ITS World Congress, NEC will use domestic and global case studies, videos, and panels to introduce a solution that combines three core technologies to achieve next-generation traffic control integrated with physical AI on expressways: (1) digital twin data-fusion technology, (2) wrong-way driving detection utilizing fiber-optic sensing, and (3) individual vehicle monitoring technology using long-range LiDAR for driving safety support.

These technologies will advance the evolution of social infrastructure, including distributed edge AI processing platforms, by enabling spatiotemporal synchronization of sensor data collected across wide areas using fiber-optic sensing.

(1) Road State Monitoring with Multimodal Sensing

On a digital twin platform with real-time spatiotemporal synchronization, data fusion technology enables both real-time, detailed monitoring of road environments and the intelligent transformation of regional road networks.

(2) Wrong-way Driving Detection Using Distributed Fiber-Optic Sensing

By utilizing continuous sensing along an entire route, monitoring blind spots can be eliminated. This allows for the collection of early warning information, enabling early detection of unforeseen circumstances, such as vehicles traveling in the wrong direction or obstacles on the road. In addition, traffic flow and safety are improved by alerting following vehicles to take evasive action.

(3) LiDAR Sensing Technology for Driving Safety Support on Expressways

Capable of capturing 3D expressway information in real time, LiDAR technology is used to detect and track moving vehicles while quickly providing traffic condition updates to autonomous and other vehicles, thus promoting safe driving. The results of field trials conducted on expressways will also be presented during the poster presentation and at the booth exhibit featuring the accepted technical paper.

Going forward, NEC will leverage its ICT infrastructure technology and proprietary analytical AI to deliver digital infrastructure for the AI Transformation (AX*) era. This infrastructure will enable the deployment of physical AI across regional road networks through digital twins that are spatiotemporally synchronized in real time.

(*) AI Transformation (AX) refers to initiatives that go beyond simply implementing AI as a tool. Instead, AX involves reshaping business processes, business models, and organizational culture based on AI.

About NEC

The NEC Group leverages technology to create social value and promote a more sustainable world where everyone has the chance to reach their full potential. NEC Corporation was established in 1899. Today, the NEC Group's approximately 110,000 employees utilize world-leading AI, security, and communications technologies to solve the most pressing needs of customers and society.

For more information, please visit https://www.nec.com, and follow us on LinkedIn and YouTube.
